reviews.text: slime kept

My copy was provided by the developer Slightly unconventional rogue-lite with a couple of original ideas, it might be a little confusing at first because it handles the loop differently from similar games, but generally I thought it was a good game with many fun unlocks. Apparently it was in development for 5 years, so that would explain why it has so many rogue-lite events and features, even though it has a very simple aesthetic to it, you'll find most of the things like unlocking skins, unlocking weapons, as well as all kinds of mini-games and upgrades. The game mainly has 2 unusual features, one is management of resources between yourself and your slime buddy, and the other is having a choice to when you want to fight a final boss, essentially allowing you to play the game until you are comfortable enough to beat him. There is only one thing that I think could be done a lot better, and that is just a lack of loop scaling for the people that might want it. So what happens is that you can beat the game once, and after that it unlocks a "challenge mode" that cycles one negative effect per day, and if I am not mistaken it may have given the boss a few new patterns. So after a few easy runs you pretty much saw the extent of the challenge that this game has to offer, and frankly the game is extremely easy. The game is still fun for those 2 runs because it has so many random rogue-lite events, but again, if you beat it once, you can it do it again with little effort, so if you are looking for that replay value, right now it's largely supported by unlocks and achievements, not by actual difficulty modifications. This is definitely something that might be an easy feature to improve, but I am just not sure if it's me, or perhaps the community is not as interested in it. The variety of unlocks and rogue-lite events is probably the strongest part of the game, even though the game is easy, you will continuously run into things that you never seen before, as well as having some decently made optional bosses. I didn't have any big complaints with the gameplay or timing, for the most part it plays perfectly fine, aside from occasional visibility issues, the game is mostly green so it's easy to mistake your pet for unfriendly slime, or fall into a hole because you thought it was a black wall tile. [h1] Pros: [/h1] (+) Many rogue-lite events, such as finding rooms with specific purpose or mini-games, basic things like shops, but also mini-bosses and other side quests (+) Good number of unlocks, skins for the character, new weapons, as well as a few extra features like the arena mode and the challenge mode. Decent achievement support (+) Had some hidden/charming moments, you may or may not run into them, but the dev plays around with your expectations a little bit (+) A few original ideas, you can toss your guns to your pet, as well as capture enemies to upgrade him instead of yourself (+) Gameplay/timing is generally good, fair difficulty [h1] Feedback: [/h1] [u]Rogue-lite Loop Scaling/Offering more optional challenge[/u] - what I would recommend personally, instead of having a 'challenge mode', have a panel that has 5 levels of 'challenge mode' that unlock one after another, and that will give the player incentive to continuously replay the game and optimize for higher challenge if desired. For example after beating the first challenge mode, the second one could have 2 negative effects at the same time, as well as 20%+ more enemy and boss health, with more enemies around the boss. In my experience there will be people that will look for something like that, and you have so many events in the game, but no difficulty scaling to optimize those strategies. And also you can add another achievement for each level for motivation. [u] Arena mode feels kinda stale [/u] - I feel like you could decrease the cost of guns in the arena mode by half, and maybe drop 25% ammo upon completing every wave, otherwise you encourage to use your pistol instead. Also I just don't find it very fun, you get 2 random choices, but maybe you could implement more features from the core game into it, have more things you could risk and reward in between the waves. [u] Slight visibility issues [/u] - the game is again, mostly green, and it looks fine, I just keep shooting my slime because I lose track of it. Your pits look a bit like walls to me as well. Maybe you could add something for the buddy to make him stand out more, something even optional in the settings, hell, just let me recolor him to yellow or white or something. On a side note, the only negative effect that really annoys me is the scythe spam, I would always skip it because it often starts on the edges of the walls and makes it dreadful to play the game, sometimes I can see it, sometime I can't. Also ideally try to write dialogue so it just pops on the screen, instead of locking character into a conversation, it's a rogue-lite, not a visual novel, keep the pacing up, cut the easy tutorials out like how to click on the dart, stop holding the hand. [b] Overall Thoughts: 8/10 [/b] I do think the game feels great for those first 2 runs because there are so many events, but it does not have more challenge after that, and for me personally, those difficulty mods is what makes me replay rogue-lites, not having more achievements or just running into more things, well after I find the game too forgiving. You have a lot of features in the game yes, and technically you have enough of them to support a game with more loop scaling, so something to consider. It plays well, it has many charming mechanics and events, but again, that challenge mode and arena mode need more thought to it, what are you actually doing if the player finds the game too easy, you have so many ways to optimize your build, but no reason to do so because the game never got challenging enough. [i] I expected 2D Slime Rancher, I received Game Boy-era The Binding of Isaac. With a store named ‘Slimeazon’, weapons like a banjo or a fish, and a pet slime which you can gift a bazooka, what’s not to love? Slimekeep oozes charm, delivering a short but satisfying experience. [/i] [h1]📝 Main Pros, Cons, and Suggestions, followed by the Review:[/h1] 🟩 Pros: + Mini bosses offer a tough but fair challenge + You get to decide when to face the final boss + The Slime King boss fight is a real test of skill + 24 helpful items to discover and enhance your runs + Bangin’ upbeat soundtrack which keeps the energy high + Capturing slimes is more engaging and interactive than expected + Huge arsenal of 42 weapons to unlock, including a banjo and a fish + Dropping weapons for your pet slime to use is a clever and satisfying mechanic + Great balance between capturing and defeating slimes to juggle resources and upgrades for both you and your slime buddy + Full control over bloom, saturation, and hue means you won’t get destroy your retinas with the radioactive slime green glow 🟥 Cons: - Slime upgrade pool is a bit too limited - You can’t cancel your special ability once it’s active - Capturing slimes is disabled while your special is running - Mini bosses can become damage sponges if you haven’t upgraded your weapons 🏷️ Suggestions: ~ Keep building on the game’s strong foundation with more content ~ Add difficulty modifiers to boost replayability and cater to different skill levels [h1] Slimekeep Oozes Charm [/h1] Slimekeep is a 16-day journey where you begin with nothing but a pistol in hand and a pet slime by your side. It opens with a brief tutorial before dropping you into what seems like the main game. This however is only a shooting range – To begin your run, you’ll need to interact with the bed. You’ll explore a series of rooms filled with enemies, events, and scaling difficulty. As days progress, stronger slimes spawn appear, bringing with them greater rewards. The goal? Find the boat room and take on the Slime King, the game’s final boss. You can challenge him whenever you feel ready, however, the longer you wait, the more slimeballs it costs to rent. Being the gaming god that I am, I obviously challenged him on Day 1. You’re probably thinking, “There’s no way you could have beaten the game on your first ever run!” And you’re 100% right. The moment the King started jumping, it was over in seconds [spoiler]not to be confused with my bedroom performance[/spoiler]. Naturally, I figured with a few more well-timed dodges, I’d clearly succeed – Nope. The second time around, the King had completely new mechanics. My stubborn self was defeated yet again, so I proceeded to play slower, only for the first mini boss to beat me down as hard as the King did. Battered and bruised, I put the game down to write this review. I am not a gamer god, heck, I’m barely a gamer at this point. I am crushed, defeated, yet I want more. Slimekeep oozes charm and delivers a short but satisfying experience. If you enjoy roguelikes, check it out – It may lack the depth and variety of others, but it more than makes up for it in charm and fun. It's got nice visuals. But I can't really give it a thumbs up for the gameplay. It has you killing slimes, but in order to get upgrades you have to NOT kill them but instead absorb them with a different gun, in a gimmicky way that's not really fun to do. Reloading is kinda annoying too and needs to be done manually. You can hold the button down to autofire but if you do this it won't auto reload and you just stop shooting. The pet slime is a fun idea but kinda meh in practice. Then the bosses are super tanky and it's sometimes unclear if/where/when you can avoid their attacks. Which, given your own limited life bar, can result in game-overs pretty quickly. The music in the (non-boss) areas is mostly just the same track on repeat and it gets annoying. And I also ran into some bugs where the pet slime AI seems to break and it just runs off, or where the absorb minigame doesn't show the catch bar after the sucky part.

Listen, all respect in the WORLD for this indie game, but i just don't really love the mechanics in this game. Slimekeep is a cute roguelike game that has a good presentation and cute graphics, i personally don't mind the presentation of the game being focused in a single color. However, after a few hours of gameplay, i can certainly assure you, there isn't much beyond the cute graphics, which is a shame for an indie game with such ambition. The weapons blend in together and they all do basically the same thing, the powers are hard to get and once your fuel for the special weapon is gone, you better hope that you got enough money to buy the refill. Some achievements and game mechanics are simply confusing and not really well explained to the player and while im not against a difficult challeng in my video games, the gameplay loop is simply too tedious and boring for me to figure everything out. This is a fun game for the first few hours, but its shallow and lacks interesting ideas that most roguelikes have to keep the player on their toes. im leaving a like on this review, but i don't really recommend the game, I just like to support indie devs.

Truth be told it just doesn't seem like a game that was worked on for as long as it did. But I don't want to slander Benbonk for that, his life was busy and that's understandable. I want to support indie devs and I'll continue playing Benbonk's games, this one just wasn't there for me. Im hoping that in the future, however, one of them will be. Thanks for all you do for us Benbonk and keep making games!
